frequency_question: How often do sovereign debt managers successfully scale up announced structural debt purchase operations to their targeted or expanded volumes without retrenching below operational thresholds?
membership_rule: Includes formalized structural Treasury/central bank buyback or large-scale programmatic intervention initiatives initiated by G7 fiscal authorities since 2000. Excludes one-off emergency crisis interventions.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Permanent Open Market Operations (POMO) scaling post-GFC
Bank of Japan JGB purchase program expansions under Kuroda
UK Debt Management Office gilt purchase operations adjustments
Federal Reserve Treasury buyback pilot program scaling
ECB Public Sector Purchase Programme volume scaling

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named major programmatic scaling precedents; covers the relevant class of sovereign debt management volume expansions.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market sovereign programs where institutional capacity might differ.
skeleton: 5 major structural sovereign/central bank liquidity program scaling instances evaluated for full implementation of target operational volumes.
validity_reason: Sovereign debt management operational scaling behaviors remain highly stable across normal and low-interest-rate regimes.
